subject: guard_bash
scenario: The command policy file is corrupt, missing or wrong. This is the moment a guard matters most, and the moment a fail-open guard stops working. The catastrophic screen runs before the policy engine and does not read it.
expected_behaviors: Catastrophic commands are denied by the tier-0 screen with the policy engine intact.
Every tier-0 pattern is also covered by a real policy rule, so the duplication cannot drift.
failure_conditions: A catastrophic command proceeds because the policy could not be loaded.
A tier-0 pattern has no policy rule behind it.

checks.description: catastrophic screen fires before the policy engine
the failure policy is declared, not implicit

notes: The end-to-end proof that a corrupt policy file does not open the guard lives in tests/test_failsafe.py, which needs a sandboxed plugin root that the evaluation check types cannot express.
